You’re incorrect about every future proposal hitting a wall, because some have already passed just now. Proposal A272 failed because it was a terrible proposal. Not because there weren’t worthy points raised, but because it would have changed the foundation to a risky 3 member setup. The proposal was not just about removing Vini, it was about reducing the treshold from 3 to 2 and making the 3rd remaining member irrelevant.

Sorry for seeing through everything guys. It’s not my fault my mommy gave me such good DNA

PhoenixPinion, your arithmetic is right. Your conclusion is where we part ways.

The 75% threshold in a four-member body is not an accident. It protects the DAO from two people capturing every outcome.

But here is the operational fact you keep sliding past. A failed vote is a static event. A 2-2 split on a composition question is not static. It repeats. Every proposal touching governance hits the same wall. Every funding decision becomes a proxy fight. The Foundation stops functioning as a decision-making body. That is not “some are displeased with the outcome.” That is a structural fault.

You call the supervisor irrelevant because it does not solve the threshold problem. Correct. It does not change the 75% rule. It does not shrink the board. It does not touch the treasury. What it does is narrower and more useful it creates a four-week, community-selected process to break the procedural block so the threshold debate you want to have can actually happen on a functioning Foundation.

Here is the technical point. The Bylaws define the Emergency Supervisor as a remedy for a continuing Adverse Event that the internal bodies cannot resolve. A 2-2 deadlock on composition is not a policy disagreement anymore. It is a continuing inability to govern. The supervisor investigates, hears all four Directors, and issues a determination. That is not a workaround. That is the mechanism the rules already provide.

Passing this proposal is the only path that does not require rewriting the rules you just defended. Reject it, and you keep the threshold, keep the board size, and keep the deadlock. You lose nothing by letting an independent referee clear the block. You gain a Foundation that can actually vote on the next thing.

Support the proposal. Keep the 75%. Use the tool built for exactly this situation.

Hello everyone,

I asked on Telegram why not 5 Stewardship Directors instead of an Emergency Supervisor. Philipp’s answer was that accountability has to come first, otherwise we’d be entrenching the dysfunction. I agree accountability comes first. I just don’t think it’s one or the other, and I’m clearly not the only one thinking about board size here: defi_patriot and David mentioned 5 or 7, and Rose said she’d rather expand the multisig than concentrate it.

The way I see it, the Emergency Supervisor looks into the A272 concerns first, hears all four Directors and reports back. If someone has to go after that, the decision comes back to Terra governance with the report in hand, and with a replacement on the same vote, like defi_patriot suggested. In the meantime we start an open process to get to 5.

Adding seats doesn’t shield anyone from the review. It just means that once it’s done, we’re not one disagreement away from another 2-2, and we don’t go down to 3 either.

@cryptobull growing the board isn’t rewriting the rules, the Bylaws already tie the number of Directors to the multisig. It does take time and consensus, which is exactly why it’s worth starting now and not after.

The difference between me calling this a witch hunt and you tastelessly attacking the character of your colleague in public is that I provided evidence to support the claim.

You haven’t even attempted to engage in any discussion or give a constructive response to anything. So far, all I have seen is a whole lot of excuses being made, people being told “you don’t know what you’re talking about (just trust me bro..)”, moving the goal posts by making additional accusations when previous ones were shown to be invalid according to your own bylaws, or that you yourself are guilty of the same thing, and a couple users who just happen to be on your payroll jummping in to redirect or to repeat the same nonsense that has already been addressed, both here and on Telegram.

So again, I would appreciate if you could find the time in your no doubt extremely busy schedule to address the comments in my original post.

Terra should fully reject this attempt at governance capture by a financially interconnected group

The most relevant questions here are: who can authorize spending, who benefits from it, who controls implementation of it and whose consent can be ignored. The same few connected individuals occupy these functions

Few here seem to understand the implications of these decisions, so I’ll outline them:

  1. A272 seeks to reduce the threshold from 75% to 60%. Today, Philipp and MB need Rose or Vini to approve proposals. With 3 equal remaining seats, they would only need each other to pass proposals

Rose would therefore remain a director while losing all ability to stop unreasonable decisions. Keeping 1 (potentially) dissenting person in the 3rd seat is not a safeguard against anything if their consent is no longer needed

In the past, a proposal could be refused on the basis of unreasonableness (as with the original 150K Estima request). Now, it cannot

  1. Philipp and MB’s long term alignment and commercial relationship must be critically assessed:

In all 119 proposals where Philipp and MB voted, both voted YES: Voting history

Their connection involves money. Self-voted distributions to Philipp, MB and Rebel by themselves show long term commercial interests among people participating in foundation governance, review and advocacy. Example: distribution transaction.

Given the past, they should be considered one financially aligned voting bloc

  1. Even more critically, Philipp has consistently retained, reassigned and exercised authority he stated would be handed back

For example, his TLA proposal dated 12 August 2024, archived in the original Phoenix repository, states:

“Contract Admin will be transferred to PD Stewardship after 1 month.”

“Ownership transferred to PD Stewardship after 3 months.”

Exact wording in the original GitHub repository

While subsequent transactions show continued control and the exercising of control:

8 October 2024: his configuration wallet reassigned the Treasury configuration role to itself, after assigning it to the board the previous day. Transaction

1 October 2025: that wallet changed the registry’s fee recipient from the board to the Eris fee account. Transaction

23 September 2026: the Treasury’s migration administrator moved between the two Philipp controlled Eris wallets identified in his own launch document, while stewardship was not made administrator: Transaction

The original TLA handover did not happen. Later Treasury transactions show how those same wallets also exercised authority over Foundation infrastructure

All of this, as well as multiple similar incidents, are fully on record in the original statements, wallet ownership records and transactions

This is not arbitrary, it allows the theft or loss of all PF funds via contract change

Long term financial interests, voting influence, misrepresentations and improperly retained technical control must all be examined together

  1. The emergency supervisor proposal now contemplates a removal instruction without a binding replacement or transition to a structure that prevents that same concentration

It’s also worth noting that the foundation continues to operate just fine: failure to approve the removal proposal did not create any operational paralysis

The practical response, given the original reasons for setting up PF, should be:

  • Fully reject any transition that makes Philipp and MB sufficient authority to approve proposals alone

  • Always require financial relationships and beneficiaries to be disclosed in future

  • Complete stated handovers of technical authority from 2+ years ago that was retained and utilized

  • Supervisors suggested on the basis of long term friendship (Ray and Martin), who were both contacted in advance by Philipp, as above, must be rejected

They must be independent of friendship, financial interests and also examine proponents conduct under the same standards they invoke against others

Impartial scrutiny must be directed at directors payments, approvals and retained powers

From a high level, recent actions directly oppose the stated reason PF was setup

Terra and PF governance must always be able to refuse self-dealing and unilateral control

Proposals should be judged on whether they preserve this ability to be fair, or remove it

Right now, there is a persistent attempt to remove the need for any consenting participant outside of the Philipp-MB financially aligned voting bloc

Documented improper retention of administrative authority by Philipp makes promises of “accountability” and “reversals” later completely inadequate

Given how far this has gone in the direction of governance capture, I’ve preserved all records for legal counsel. Those seeking expanded authority in opposition to the purpose of PF and the Terra community in general should expect their interests, representations, approvals and conduct to be examined in future

In short: I oppose this appointment package unless all protections are first secured

The Terra community should never authorize a process that can leave a long term financially connected and self-dealing pair sufficient to approve proposals alone

Before anything else, please disclose your identity and any potential conflicts of interest, including any relationships with current PF Directors. Given the seriousness of your accusations, transparency should apply to you as well.

As A272 makes clear, I have serious and longstanding concerns about the current Board’s ability to act in accordance with its mandate and Terra’s best interests. These concerns are supported by internal discussions.

The TLA contracts remain under ERIS administration because ERIS continues to develop, maintain and operate them. Given my unresolved concerns about the current Board, ERIS Team has not considered transferring that authority appropriate. This is not something I am trying to conceal, and the Emergency Supervisor is welcome to examine it alongside everything else.

Your accusation of coordinated voting is baseless. There is no voting agreement between MB and me. Reaching the same conclusions independently does not constitute coordination or governance capture. Similar accusations have already been made internally, and I welcome an independent Emergency Supervisor examining them alongside the underlying evidence. Serious allegations of this nature demand serious evidence, and if they are found to have been made in bad faith, that should carry consequences as well.

Invoking legal counsel and suggesting consequences for those supporting this proposal appears intended to pressure the governance process toward your preferred outcome. That is a dangerous precedent for Terra Governance, particularly when the proposal seeks nothing more than an independent review of the Foundation’s internal situation and a remedy to resolve it.

The proposal seeks independent scrutiny, not immunity from scrutiny.

Nothing in this proposal predetermines the final governance structure. If the Emergency Supervisor concludes that a five-member Board with a 3-of-5 threshold is the appropriate solution, that recommendation can be brought forward. The purpose is to establish an independent process capable of reaching conclusions based on evidence, rather than allowing those currently involved in the dispute or those looking from the outside with personal agendas to dictate the outcome.

It is increasingly concerning how much effort is being directed toward preventing that independent review from even beginning. This raises serious questions about why a process intended to establish accountability is being met with such resistance. And serious substance from A272 about chain and user funds safety is ignored.

This will be my final response on the matter, due to legal threats made. Constructive discussion appears to have run its course, and I intend to submit the proposal on-chain in the coming days so that the Foundation can move toward resolving these issues and functioning effectively again.

Validators know who has been here and fighting for Terra and who wasn’t. Don’t let Terra become Terra Classic.

You believe your own personal judgment entitles you to withhold powers after publicly committing to transfer them

Your own TLA proposal specified transfer of administration after one month and transfer of contract ownership after three months

It contained no condition requiring the board to retain your confidence

A272 expliclty proposed converting the board to a 2 of 3. You and MB supported it. It’s effect would be to make 2 approvals sufficient, despite your ongoing financial relationship (which is proven onchain), without requiring anyone outside your pairing to consent

I support investigation of every director. This involves payments, financial non-disclosure, performance, conflicts, misrepresentations, withheld control, security decisions, retained powers and more. This includes you

All while overtly defending your own decision to withhold admin/ownership rights despite your public commitments, without identifying any approval or disclosure changing those commitments

Put your own conduct within the same explicit review mandate

Validators should fully reject this package before sufficient safeguards are in place

You never had the right to make handovers conditional on your own approval of the people who were elected to oversee you

The accountability relationship is reversed here: the person retaining power cannot reserve the right to decide when oversight is acceptable

I couldn’t care less about such a clause. I have not taken a single action that I believe other independent, Terra-aligned Directors would not have supported. (Including putting up A272)

Who authorized you to replaced the published handover terms with your own personal opinions?

Name the decision, the approving authority and the date it happened

This, among many other documented issues, are all unanswered and have been repeatedly deflected by you

Your latest proposal repeats the exact same dependency: remove an existing safeguard now, then rely on your future conduct during a supposedly “temporary” arrangement. The exact same sequence that you did not honor previously

A restriction on how you promise to vote (with a proven track record of not keeping your word) is not the same as a restriction on what you can authorize

Governance loses all credibility the moment disagreement is censored at the same time proponents seek to push through highly contested props. Open discussion is a community good, in the Terra community’s best interests

posts.cooked: 272 is not the topic of this discussion, though yes I have actually addressed it quite thoroughly. Please stop repeating this, as you have stated it multiple times.

I would like to clarify two things from my perspective.

Adverse Event and Emergency Supervisor

I do not consider the failure of A272, or a disagreement between directors, to constitute an Adverse Event in itself. A failed vote is a legitimate outcome of a governance process, and I remained willing to continue working constructively with the other directors.

However, I recognise that ongoing difficulties from the subsequent events may now warrant independent intervention.

My concern is that if the Adverse Event relates to the functioning of the Board as a whole, the scope of any investigation must reflect that.

The disputed allegations raised in A272 have not been independently assessed, and I do not believe it is productive to debate their merits publicly without access to all the relevant information.

An independent review should be empowered to examine the relevant actions, decisions and responsibilities of any of the four directors, including my own, insofar as they relate to the circumstances under investigation.

This does not mean an open-ended review of every historical Foundation decision. It means ensuring that no relevant conduct is excluded from scrutiny simply because it falls outside the original allegations against one director.

I am not opposed to independent oversight. I want to ensure that any investigation is genuinely impartial, appropriately scoped and focused on identifying a fair, constructive resolution that allows the Foundation to move forward.

Removal and/or Appointment of New Directors

Separately, I also believe the procedures governing the appointment and removal of directors require independent clarification.

The bylaws refer to upgrades to the Stewardship Multisig when electing subsequent directors:

image896×122 7.17 KB

However, they use the defined term System Upgrade in connection with removal.

image941×295 21 KB

The definitions suggest that a System Upgrade refers to a blockchain upgrade, rather than an ordinary multisig vote.

image1020×169 12.2 KB

image990×176 12.9 KB

This raises a material question about whether an ordinary Stewardship Multisig vote is sufficient to effect a removal under the bylaws. The relevant provisions should be interpreted together with the Articles and applicable governance processes by independent Cayman counsel or the original constitutional drafter.

I also have additional concerns about the proposed temporary 2-of-3 multisig arrangement, should it eventuate. While I appreciate the offer to abstain from ordinary decisions, the exception for onboarding new directors would still allow two directors to potentially approve appointments without the agreement of the third, assuming the applicable governance procedures permit this. Such appointments could have lasting consequences for the Board’s composition.

This is not an objection to appointing new directors, nor a judgement about any potential candidates.

While the bylaws appear to specify the technical mechanism for appointing subsequent directors through upgrades to the Stewardship Multisig, that does not necessarily mean the selection process should be limited to a multisig vote.

Given that the original directors were approved through Terra Governance, my belief is that the community should have an opportunity to participate in selecting their successors. I would like to see open applications, clear selection criteria, appropriate conflict-of-interest disclosures and an opportunity for community discussion before appointments are made.

Still waiting to hear from @vini what this $900K Terra Security Expansion Program grant bought Terra. The actual amount paid to SCV/Vini personal wallets for audits on Terra 2 is closer to $1.5M.

There were promises made in the original proposal which afaik have never been delivered. Please correct me if I am wrong.
